title: Simulacro 20 — UX de productos IA + GEO/AEO: posicionar en respuestas de IA
focus: Diseñar productos IA que la gente confíe (human-in-the-loop, confidence, error handling) + GEO/AEO — cómo tu página sale primero cuando alguien pregunta a una IA.

questions.scenario: Tu equipo lanza un chatbot de soporte. El PM quiere: 'siempre respuesta directa, nunca digas no sé'. Un dev UX responde: 'esto va a explotar en la cara cuando el modelo alucine'.
questions.question: ¿Cuál es el approach correcto para diseñar UX que refleje incertidumbre del modelo?

options.text: El modelo TIENE incertidumbre; ocultarla erosiona confianza cuando errors emergen. Design patterns: (1) CONFIDENCE indicators (thermometer, badge, o texto 'high/medium/low confidence'); (2) SOURCE CITATIONS obligatorias (link a docs, quotes); (3) GRACEFUL 'I don't know' con handoff a humano; (4) HEDGING language cuando apropiado ('parece que', 'según X source'); (5) SHOW WORK para tasks complejos (thinking, reasoning steps). El usuario informado confía MÁS a largo plazo que el usuario mentido a corto plazo.
options.why: Correcto. Es el consenso post-2024 sobre AI UX. Overconfidence + hallucination es el killer de trust. Los productos IA mejores (Perplexity, ChatGPT search, Copilot) muestran citations obligatorias y hedging cuando apropiado. Anthropic publicó guidelines explícitas sobre 'appropriate confidence'.

options.text: El PM tiene razón: hedging confunde al usuario.
options.why: Falso. Estudios (Google, MSFT Research 2023-2025) muestran que hedging + citations aumentan trust y task completion. El costo es 'menos punchy' pero el benefit es enorme.

options.text: Mostrar 'I don't know' sin más options es user experience mediocre.
options.why: Correcto si es SIN handoff. Pero 'I don't know + here's a link + here's a human option' es superior a fake certainty.

options.text: Usuarios prefieren respuestas ambiguas siempre.
options.why: Falso. La regla es 'calibrated confidence' — confidence alta cuando apropiado, baja cuando apropiado. No 'siempre ambiguo'.

questions.explanation: Design principles para AI UX bajo incertidumbre: (1) CALIBRATED confidence — model's certainty debe reflejarse en UI; (2) TRANSPARENCY — sources visible, provenance clara; (3) GRACEFUL FALLBACK — 'I don't know' + human handoff, no fabricación; (4) HEDGING language cuando apropiado ('parece que', 'según X', 'no estoy seguro pero'); (5) EDITABLE outputs — user puede corregir sin fricción; (6) UNDO obligatorio para actions with consequences. Reference: Google PAIR (People + AI Research) guidebook, Microsoft Human-AI Interaction Guidelines (Amershi et al. 2019 — 18 rules). El anti-patrón: 'sound authoritative always'.
questions.realWorld: Perplexity muestra sources numeradas en cada respuesta — key differentiator vs ChatGPT original. Google AI Overviews mostró 'glue on pizza' incident (2024) por no hedge cuando source era joke. ChatGPT search 2024 añadió source cards mandatory. Klarna AI chatbot 2024 tuvo backlash inicial por fake confidence y ajustaron.

references.title: Amershi et al. — Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction (2019)

questions.scenario: Tu producto usa AI para enviar emails de outreach. Debate: '¿el AI envía directo o requiere approval humano?'. PM: 'approval mata la velocidad'. UX: 'sin approval, un error borra reputación'.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son los patterns de human-in-the-loop y cómo elegir?

options.text: Patterns por nivel de autonomía: (1) FULLY AUTONOMOUS — AI actúa sin approval (justificado si acción reversible, low-stakes, high volume); (2) APPROVE-THEN-ACT — human clicks approve antes de send (default para acciones con consequences externas); (3) EDIT-THEN-SUBMIT — AI drafts, human edita y submite (best UX para content creation); (4) SUGGEST-ONLY — AI muestra opciones, human elige (para decisiones importantes); (5) UNDO WINDOW — AI actúa pero permite reverse por N segundos (Gmail undo send). Elección por: reversibility, blast radius, user expertise, time sensitivity.
options.why: Correcto. Human-in-the-loop no es binario. Los 5 patterns cubren el espectro. Edit-then-submit es el sweet spot para emails/content (velocity + safety). Fully autonomous solo para acciones truly reversible/low-stakes. Elegir bien evita ambos extremos (bottleneck vs disaster).

options.text: Siempre human approval; safety first.
options.why: Overhead innecesario para tasks reversible/low-stakes. Y crea bottleneck que reduce adoption.

options.text: Siempre fully autonomous; AI es más rápido.
options.why: Ignora consequences irreversibles. Un email malo enviado a 10k clientes tiene reputation cost enorme.

options.text: Depende del modelo; con GPT-5 no necesitas humans.
options.why: Ni GPT-5 ni Claude tienen 100% reliability. Human-in-the-loop es hedge contra fallo del modelo, no reflejo de calidad del modelo.

questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop patterns matrix: 5 patterns por (a) reversibility, (b) blast radius. Fully autonomous OK si: reversible + low blast + high volume (e.g., spam filter classification). Approve-then-act para: external actions with consequences (send email, make payment, deploy code). Edit-then-submit para: content creation (email drafts, documents). Suggest-only para: decisions with judgment (which candidate to interview). Undo window para: async actions (Gmail send undo 30s). Anti-patterns: (1) approval theater (human clicks without reading — automation bias); (2) no undo for consequential actions; (3) inconsistent pattern (users don't know what to expect). Reference: Google PAIR People + AI Guidebook, sección 'Feedback + Control'.
questions.realWorld: GitHub Copilot: edit-then-submit (suggests, dev accepts). Cursor: same. Claude Code: multiple patterns depending on task type. Zapier Zaps: mix (some autonomous, others need approval). Gmail undo send: undo window pattern established. Notion AI writing: edit-then-submit.

references.title: Google PAIR — People + AI Guidebook (Feedback + Control)

questions.scenario: Tu producto muestra una spinner de 30 segundos mientras el modelo responde. Users reportan: 'parece congelado, cierro el tab'. Un dev sugiere 'usemos streaming para mostrar la respuesta a medida que llega'. Otro: 'también mostremos el reasoning intermedio como Claude/o1'.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son las opciones y trade-offs?

options.text: Progressive disclosure de output: (1) STREAMING tokens — muestra respuesta a medida que llega (SSE, WebSocket). Reduce percepción de latency dramáticamente. Trivial de implementar; users lo esperan; (2) THINKING/REASONING visible (o1, Claude thinking) — muestra proceso intermedio antes de respuesta final. Aumenta trust (ver 'cómo piensa'); útil en tasks complejas; trade-off: ocupa espacio, puede confundir en tasks simples; (3) STAGED updates (para agents multi-step) — 'searching docs... found 5... generating answer...'. Ambos: no perfect, elegir por use case.
options.why: Correcto. Streaming es table-stakes en 2026. Thinking visible es diferenciador en tasks complejos donde 'ver el reasoning' añade valor. Anti-pattern: spinner sin feedback que causa abandonment.

options.text: Solo mostrar resultado final; el proceso intermedio distrae.
options.why: Falso. 30 segundos sin feedback destroys UX. Los users perceived latency es distinta de actual latency; feedback intermedio reduce percepción incluso si actual es igual.

options.text: Siempre streaming + siempre thinking visible.
options.why: Streaming: sí. Thinking visible: depende. Para 'what's the weather' mostrar 5 líneas de reasoning es ruido. Para 'debug this code' es valioso. Adapt por task type.

options.text: Streaming es solo para chatbots; APIs no lo necesitan.
options.why: Falso. Server-sent events (SSE) es útil también en APIs — permite consumer procesar chunks (early rendering, cancel si obviously wrong). Anthropic, OpenAI, Google APIs todas support streaming.

questions.explanation: Streaming implementation: SSE (Server-Sent Events) más simple que WebSocket para one-way stream. Anthropic/OpenAI/Google APIs support streaming. Thinking visible: introduced by o1 (Sep 2024) y Claude 3.7/Sonnet thinking mode (2025). Trade-offs: (a) latency perceived reduction, (b) trust increase (visible reasoning), (c) UI real estate, (d) users occasionally read reasoning y catch model errors. Design: collapsable thinking, prominent answer. Anti-pattern: hidden loading state (spinner) sin progress feedback for long ops. Nielsen's response time limits: 0.1s instant, 1s stay focused, 10s attention limit — beyond 10s, need progress indicator.
questions.realWorld: ChatGPT streaming since launch (Nov 2022). Claude, Gemini, Perplexity all stream. o1 thinking visible (Sep 2024) was novel, adopted by Claude thinking, DeepSeek R1, Gemini reasoning modes. Cursor 'chat' streams. Perplexity 'searching web...' staged updates.

questions.topic: Manejo de errores — fallbacks vs technical errors
questions.scenario: Tu chatbot ocasionalmente falla: rate limit del vendor, timeout, contexto que excede tokens, safety filter block. Options: (a) mostrar 'Error: 429 rate limit exceeded'; (b) 'Sorry, something went wrong'; (c) 'I need a moment, let me try again' + auto-retry; (d) 'This is beyond what I can help with right now, let me connect you with a human'.
questions.question: ¿Cuál es la estrategia correcta de manejo de errores?

options.text: Depende del tipo de error: (1) TRANSIENT (rate limit, timeout) → auto-retry con backoff, silent al user si succeeds; si sigue fallando, mensaje friendly 'un momento, reintentando'; (2) CONTEXT EXCEEDED → summarize history y continue transparente; (3) SAFETY BLOCK → mensaje empático explicando (no exponer 'safety filter fired'); (4) UNKNOWN → generic apology + escalation to human; (5) NUNCA exponer HTTP codes, stack traces, o vendor names a end-users. Log detalles internamente para debugging.
options.why: Correcto. Diferenciar por type es key. Auto-retry transparent para transient; explanation friendly para permanentes; human handoff cuando apropiado. Exponer HTTP 429 al user es unprofessional y unhelpful. Log rich internally para debug, mostrar friendly externally.

options.text: Siempre 'Something went wrong'.
options.why: Info leakage vacío; user no sabe si retry ayuda, si es su culpa, si contactar support. Genérico frustra.

options.text: Siempre exponer HTTP codes for transparency.
options.why: Users no técnicos no entienden 429. Info leakage sin utilidad. Y expone vendor stack. Log internally, transformar externally.

options.text: Los errores son responsabilidad del user; explicar poco.
options.why: Actitud incorrecta. Errores del sistema son de todos, especialmente del provider. El user needs actionable info.

questions.explanation: Error handling matrix para AI products: (1) TRANSIENT (rate limit 429, timeout, temporary 5xx) — auto-retry con exponential backoff (jitter), silent si <3 attempts succeed; if all fail, message user 'un momento, reintentando'; (2) CONTEXT WINDOW EXCEEDED — apply summarization internally, continue transparently, or notify 'la conversación es larga, resumiendo contexto anterior'; (3) SAFETY BLOCK (content flagged) — message empático 'esto está fuera de lo que puedo ayudar aquí', ofrecer alternatives; (4) UNKNOWN — generic + escalation offer; (5) UPSTREAM DOWN (vendor incident) — status page link + estimated resolution. Anti-patterns: HTTP codes to end-users, stack traces, vendor names ('OpenAI is down'), tech jargon. Retry policy: idempotent operations retry safely; non-idempotent (payment, send) require careful design (idempotency keys).
questions.realWorld: ChatGPT muestra friendly errors, no 429s. Claude.ai similar. Perplexity durante outages muestra 'reconnecting' con retry. Stripe famoso por bad error messages transformados into humane (Stripe UX docs 2020+). AWS Console notoriously bad at error UX — lesson of what NOT to do.

questions.scenario: Tu app de voice assistant tiene 2s de latency entre user query y first token. Un designer propone: '(1) mostrar reflection with '...' bubble; (2) mostrar 'Listening...' → 'Thinking...' → response; (3) synthetic 'um, let me think...' from AI'.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son las mejores prácticas de latency masking?

options.text: Priorizar por autenticidad: (1) IMMEDIATE ACKNOWLEDGMENT (0-100ms) — 'listening' o typing indicator, no synthetic content; (2) HONEST STATUS (100ms-2s) — 'searching', 'thinking' when true, evita mentir; (3) STREAM AS SOON AS POSSIBLE — first token quickly reduces perceived latency drastically; (4) EVITA synthetic hesitations ('um, let me think') que engañan al user sobre lo que hace el sistema; (5) para agentes multi-step, mostrar staged progress ('searching docs... found 5... analyzing...'). Regla: reduce perceived latency, don't lie about what's happening.
options.why: Correcto. Latency masking legítimo (acknowledgment + honest status + fast first token) es apropiado. Synthetic hesitations son dark pattern (engañar al user sobre naturaleza del AI). Los mejores products (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity) usan honest indicators.

options.text: Synthetic 'um' es OK porque hace al AI parecer más humano.
options.why: Anti-pattern. Anthropomorphizing al AI para hide latency es dark pattern y erosiona trust si users se dan cuenta. Also, subtle deception can violate 'transparency' obligations (EU AI Act Art. 50).

options.text: No mostrar nada; el user espera.
options.why: 10s sin feedback = user abandonment (Nielsen). Debes indicar 'sistema procesa', si no user asume freezing.

options.text: Mostrar loading spinner es suficiente en todos los casos.
options.why: Spinner genérico peor que status-specific message ('searching docs' te dice qué pasa). Y en chats, typing indicator + streaming es superior.

questions.explanation: Latency masking honest patterns: (1) IMMEDIATE (0-100ms) — visual acknowledgment (typing dots, mic icon animation) — no content generated; (2) HONEST STATUS (100ms-2s) — 'searching', 'thinking', 'generating' — describe what system is doing; (3) STREAM ASAP — get first token to user quickly, then progressive; (4) STAGED PROGRESS for multi-step ('searching docs... found 5... generating summary...'). Anti-patterns: (a) synthetic hesitations ('um, let me think'); (b) fake progress bars; (c) generic spinner en operations >2s; (d) misleading status ('almost done' cuando es 50%). Reference: Nielsen Norman response times (0.1s instant, 1s focus, 10s abandonment). Voice assistants have extra constraint: silence >3s is uncomfortable — TTS 'let me check' OK if true.
questions.realWorld: Perplexity muestra 'Searching... Retrieved 8 sources... Reading them...' — honest staged. Google search Gemini AI Overviews immediate spinner then streams. Voice: Siri/Alexa use audible acknowledgment tones. Anti-pattern documented: Alexa temporarily used synthetic hesitations in 2023, backlash for anthropomorphism, removed.

questions.scenario: En tu chatbot, cuando el modelo empieza a generar una respuesta mala, users no tienen forma de detenerlo — deben esperar 30s a que termine. Reports: 'me da rabia ver que sigue generando basura'.
questions.question: ¿Por qué el stop button es crítico en AI UX?

options.text: Stop button es una feature de control fundamental porque: (1) usuarios detectan tempranamente cuando la respuesta va mal — deben poder abortar; (2) reduce costos (tokens no generados no se pagan); (3) reduce latency percibida (user recupera control); (4) evita frustración; (5) mandatory para safety en agentes con actions (Ctrl+C interrupt); (6) implementación: cancel abort signal del stream + notify backend. Es table-stakes en 2026; ausentarlo es UX defecto.
options.why: Correcto. Stop button es non-negotiable en AI products serios. Anthropic, OpenAI, todos lo tienen. En agentes, es incluso más crítico — un agente ejecutando actions sin stop puede causar damage. Implementación: AbortController en frontend + backend recibe cancel y para generación.

options.text: Stop button no es necesario; users deben esperar.
options.why: Contradice principio básico de user control. Nielsen Heuristic #3: 'User control and freedom'. Sin stop, users pierden control.

options.text: Stop button complica implementación por poco valor.
options.why: Falso. AbortController + backend cancel es straightforward. El valor es enorme (UX, cost, safety).

options.text: Stop button solo importa en agentes, no chats.
options.why: En chats también — interrumpir generación mala es valor. Y en agentes, es aún más crítico (safety, cost, damage prevention).

questions.explanation: Stop button implementation: (1) FRONTEND — AbortController + AbortSignal passed to fetch; (2) BACKEND — receive cancellation (SSE connection close, WebSocket disconnect), propagate to LLM provider (Anthropic/OpenAI APIs accept cancel via connection close); (3) STATE — mark request as cancelled, log tokens consumed for billing; (4) UX — button appears when generation starts, disappears when done, visual affordance (red or 'stop' icon). For AGENTS: stop must also interrupt tool calls in flight (careful with irreversible actions — need transactional design or 'safe interrupt' points). Reference Nielsen Heuristic #3 (User control and freedom), Anthropic Agent design principles.
questions.realWorld: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity all have stop button prominent. Claude Code CLI: Ctrl+C interrupt. Cursor: Escape key. Aider: Ctrl+C. Devin agent: 'pause' + 'stop' controls. Absence: some enterprise chatbots without stop — reported as UX defect.

questions.scenario: Tu SaaS charges por tokens usados. Users se sorprenden con facturas grandes. Options: (1) mostrar cost estimado por prompt antes de enviar; (2) mostrar cost cumulativo por sesión; (3) mostrar cost solo en billing dashboard mensual; (4) alertas cuando exceeds threshold.
questions.question: ¿Cuál es el approach correcto?

options.text: Multi-layer: (1) PRE-EXECUTION estimate para operations caras (dashboard, large context) — 'this will use ~15k tokens (~$0.30)'; (2) PER-SESSION running counter — 'sesión: $2.30'; (3) MONTHLY dashboard con drill-down (por feature, día, usuario); (4) ALERTS configurables (50%, 80%, 100% del budget); (5) HARD LIMITS (users set max spend per day/month). Regla: transparency proporcional al blast radius. Micro-cost per query = counter agregado; macro-cost operations = pre-execution estimate.
options.why: Correcto. Es defense-in-depth: pre-execution para operations caras (evita accidents), running counter (awareness), dashboard (historic), alerts (proactive), hard limits (safety net). Anthropic Claude console, OpenAI dashboards, Cursor todos implementan variations. Sin transparency, users tienen bill shock.

options.text: Solo mostrar en billing mensual; interrumpe UX si es intra-app.
options.why: Muy tarde. Bill shock destroys trust. Real-time awareness allows self-regulation.

options.text: Mostrar cost por token en cada respuesta.
options.why: Ruido para user. Ellos no entienden tokens; entienden $. Agregar a $ por sesión/día es lo que importa.

options.text: Cost debería ser invisible; UX es distraction.
options.why: Falso. Cost transparency es feature. Users que pagan quieren saber cuánto. Especialmente en enterprise donde budget matters.

questions.explanation: Cost transparency patterns: (1) PRE-EXECUTION estimate — muestra costo predicho antes de operations caras (analyze large repo, generate video, batch process); (2) RUNNING COUNTER — session cost visible, running total en dashboard; (3) MONTHLY dashboard — detailed breakdown per feature/user/day, exportable; (4) ALERTS — configurable thresholds notify user (50/80/100% budget); (5) HARD LIMITS — max spend cap (fail closed vs open — question of business); (6) FORECAST — 'at this rate, monthly bill will be ~$X'. UX principle: users con transparency self-regulate; sin transparency, blame vendor when bill arrives. Reference: AWS Cost Explorer, Vercel usage dashboards, Anthropic Console.
questions.realWorld: Anthropic Console shows cost real-time. OpenAI dashboards similar. Cursor $30 tier removal (2024) fue partly because users didn't see running cost. Vercel had cases of viral apps generating huge bills (2023) — added better limits. AWS 'bill shock' famous — added cost anomaly detection.

questions.scenario: Tu RAG-based product responde queries. Un competitor (Perplexity) muestra sources numeradas con quote highlighting. Tu team debate: '¿lo copiamos? ¿es mejor tener bullets sin sources? ¿footnotes?'.
questions.question: ¿Cuál es la best practice de citations en AI UX?

options.text: Citations obligatorias en RAG products porque: (1) VERIFIABILITY — user puede confirmar información; (2) TRUST — fuentes visibles = accountable; (3) LEGAL — attribution puede ser requerido (news content, academic); (4) SEO reverso — driving traffic a sources creates ecosystem sustainability. Patterns: inline numbers [1] con hover/click showing source, sidebar con sources list, quote highlighting cuando applicable, click-through to original. Perplexity setup es standard de-facto. ChatGPT search adoptó similar 2024.
options.why: Correcto. Citations son standard en RAG. Verifiability + trust + legal + ecosystem. Perplexity pioneered UX; ChatGPT search, Claude adopted. Sin citations, RAG es 'trust me bro' — no defensible.

options.text: Citations distraen; solo bullet points de respuesta.
options.why: Sacrifica trust y verifiability por marginal cleanliness. Users sophisticated (los que importan) quieren sources.

options.text: Citations solo en 'research mode', no en chat default.
options.why: Puede depender de use case, pero para RAG-based responses, citations debería ser default. Distinguir 'general chat' vs 'RAG-based response' con distinta UX.

options.text: Copiar Perplexity exactamente es plagio.
options.why: Patrones de UX no son copyright; ideas de UX son copiable. Y Perplexity setup no es único (académicos citing sources for centuries). Adoptar patrones probados es lo correcto.

questions.explanation: Citation UX patterns: (1) INLINE numbers [1][2] con hover preview + click to source (Perplexity, ChatGPT search); (2) SIDEBAR panel con list of sources, highlighted paragraph cuando cited; (3) FOOTNOTES (academic style) — más denso; (4) QUOTE HIGHLIGHTING — highlight fragment of source that was used; (5) CONFIDENCE per citation ('this fact is well-supported' vs 'inferred'). Implementation: LLM outputs citations markers, retrieval layer maps back to original chunks with URLs. Anti-patterns: citations sin verifiable link, hallucinated citations (LLM invents URLs — must validate), overwhelming (10+ citations per sentence).
questions.realWorld: Perplexity established modern citation UX pattern (2023). ChatGPT search launched Oct 2024 con source cards. Claude cites sources when tools return them. Google AI Overviews shows source thumbnails. Bing Chat/Copilot early adopter (2023) though sometimes hallucinated URLs.

questions.scenario: Tu chatbot tiene thumbs up/down en cada respuesta. Product analytics: 5% thumbs down, 2% thumbs up. PM: 'los users no usan feedback'. Data team: 'usar los thumbs down para retrainar'. Legal: '¿podemos usar user data para retrainar?'.
questions.question: ¿Cuál es el approach correcto para feedback loops?

options.text: Approach: (1) FEEDBACK RATE bajo (~5-10%) es normal — thumbs son minority signal, no majority; (2) THUMBS DOWN + optional 'why' selector (unhelpful, incorrect, harmful, other) gives structured data; (3) IMPLICIT feedback (regeneration, copy, edit, dwell time) supplements explicit; (4) LEGAL — consent explicit for training use (Terms + optional opt-in); (5) PROCESS — aggregate periodic review, categorize, use for prompt improvements / eval dataset / fine-tuning; (6) NEVER use raw feedback data with PII for training without careful sanitization.
options.why: Correcto. Feedback loops son goldmines pero requiere estructura (categorize, sanitize) y consent. Rate 5% es normal (silent majority); implicit signals suplementan. Legal es critical (GDPR + AI Act obligations). Anthropic, OpenAI publican política de user data usage para training.

options.text: Ignora feedback si rate es <20%.
options.why: 5% de 1M users = 50k signals. Rich data. Bajo rate es normal, no razón para ignorar.

options.text: Usar feedback data para retrain sin consent — es 'our data'.
options.why: GDPR + EU AI Act require legal basis + transparency + possibly opt-in. Using user data for training without proper consent = compliance risk.

options.text: Thumbs feedback es unreliable; ignorar y usar solo A/B tests.
options.why: A/B tests son complementarios, no reemplazan thumbs. Thumbs give per-response signal; A/B gives system-level signal. Ambos útiles.

questions.explanation: Feedback loop pipeline: (1) EXPLICIT (thumbs, ratings, 'why' selectors) — high signal, low volume; (2) IMPLICIT (regeneration, edit, copy, dwell, follow-up questions) — lower signal but higher volume; (3) STORAGE con PII redaction, permission tags; (4) CATEGORIZATION (unhelpful / factually wrong / harmful / off-topic / other); (5) ANALYSIS — patterns, top failure modes; (6) ACTION — prompt updates, eval dataset additions, fine-tuning candidates, RLHF; (7) LEGAL — consent para training use, opt-out mechanisms. Anti-patterns: (a) collect without consent; (b) train on PII; (c) not close the loop (users give feedback, nothing changes = they stop giving). Reference: RLHF papers, OpenAI feedback methodology.
questions.realWorld: ChatGPT thumbs feedback used for RLHF training (with consent per terms). Claude same. Copilot feedback via 'accept/reject completion'. GitHub reports millions of signals monthly. Snorkel, Argilla — tools for feedback data curation.

references.title: Ouyang et al. — Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (2022)

questions.scenario: Tu producto genera contenido con AI. Compliance dice 'debemos labelear'. Design: 'un badge grande arruina UX'. PM: 'pongámoslo minúsculo en gris al final'.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son las obligations y anti-patterns de AI content labeling?

options.text: Obligations: EU AI Act Art. 50 (aplicable Aug 2026) obliga: (1) chatbot disclosure ('estás hablando con IA' — al inicio, claramente); (2) synthetic content (imágenes, video, audio, text deepfakes) — machine-readable marking + human-perceptible label; (3) emotion recognition / biometric categorization — inform users. Anti-patterns (dark): (a) label minúsculo hidden; (b) 'opcional dismissal' que persiste hidden; (c) technical language that users don't understand ('powered by GPT-4'); (d) disclosure oculto en Terms of Service. Best practice: clear, prominent, in language users understand.
options.why: Correcto. Art. 50 aplicable Aug 2, 2026. Requirements: disclosure clear + accessible + in easy-to-understand language. Anti-patterns (dark UX) que Article específicamente combate: dismissible/hidden/technical labels. Fines up to €15M o 3% turnover for non-compliance.

options.text: Sin obligación específica; label opcional.
options.why: Falso. EU AI Act Art. 50 explícitamente obliga. Aplicable Aug 2026.

options.text: Label solo si el user pregunta.
options.why: Falso. Obligation es proactive disclosure, no on-request.

options.text: 'AI-generated' badge minúsculo cumple.
options.why: Depende del contexto y prominencia. Art. 50 requires 'in a clear and distinguishable manner'. Judges de tribunales evaluarán. Minúsculo hidden puede ser evaluado como no cumple.

questions.explanation: AI content labeling obligations (EU AI Act Art. 50, aplicable Aug 2, 2026): (1) CHATBOTS — deployers of AI systems intended to interact with natural persons debe informarles que están interacting with AI 'unless obvious from context'; (2) SYNTHETIC CONTENT — providers of GenAI must ensure output marked machine-readable (watermark, metadata) + users deben ser informed cuando content generado (deepfakes especially — 'deep fake' text label); (3) EMOTION/BIOMETRIC — inform data subjects; (4) EXCEPTIONS — art (satire, fiction), law enforcement authorized. Dark patterns to AVOID: hidden labels, dismissible-and-forget, jargon, buried in TOS. Best practice: prominent, plain language, at moment of interaction. Similar US: FTC 'AI-generated' disclosure guidance. C2PA (Content Authenticity Initiative) — technical standard for provenance.
questions.realWorld: Meta, TikTok label AI-generated content 2024+. OpenAI DALL-E adds C2PA metadata. Google SynthID watermark for AI images. Grammarly, Notion AI label generated text. Aug 2, 2026 marks Art. 50 enforcement — many products racing to comply. FTC has warned companies about deceptive AI marketing (2023-2024).

references.title: C2PA — Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity

questions.topic: Qué es GEO — Generative Engine Optimization
questions.scenario: En una reunión de marketing, el CMO dice: 'necesitamos GEO. Nuestra página no sale nunca en Perplexity o ChatGPT'. Un jr pregunta: '¿GEO es SEO?'.
questions.question: ¿Qué es GEO y en qué se diferencia de SEO?

options.text: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) — practice of structuring content para que sea CITADA por generative AI systems (ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Bing Copilot, Gemini). Diferencia con SEO: SEO optimiza para RANKING en search results tradicionales (10 blue links); GEO optimiza para ser CITED source en synthesized AI responses. Overlapping: content de calidad, structure clara, autoridad. Diferente: GEO focuses en machine parseability, citation-worthiness, factual density. AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) es sinónimo casi. También emerging: llms.txt como convención.
options.why: Correcto. GEO es discipline emergente distinta pero relacionada a SEO. Coined ~2023-2024, standardizing 2025-2026. Goal es diferente: rank vs cite. Some techniques overlap (quality content); others differ (structured data more critical for GEO, backlinks less).

options.text: GEO es solo un rebrand de SEO.
options.why: Falso. Distinto objetivo (cite en AI response vs rank en search). Distintos crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot vs Googlebot). Distintos patterns (structured markup, llms.txt vs backlinks).

options.text: GEO es imposible; los AI models son cajas negras.
options.why: Falso. Los AI models retrieval-augmented (Perplexity, ChatGPT search, Gemini) usan crawls públicos + prefer certain content. Con techniques, aumentas citation likelihood.

options.text: GEO es solo para content marketing; no aplica a SaaS.
options.why: Falso. Cualquier organization que quiera ser citada en AI answers (docs technical, product info, thought leadership) beneficia de GEO.

questions.explanation: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) definition: practice of structuring web content to be cited by generative AI systems. Related terms: AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) — mostly synonymous, some use interchangeably. GEO vs SEO comparison: (1) OBJECTIVE — SEO: rank in SERPs / GEO: be cited in AI responses; (2) MEASUREMENT — SEO: position, CTR / GEO: citation frequency, referral traffic from AI (harder to measure); (3) TECHNIQUES — SEO: keywords, backlinks, technical SEO / GEO: structured data (schema.org, JSON-LD), semantic HTML, factual density, quotable content, updated dates, llms.txt; (4) CRAWLERS — SEO: Googlebot, Bingbot / GEO: GPTBot (OpenAI), ClaudeBot (Anthropic), PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot (Common Crawl); (5) OVERLAP — quality content + clear structure benefit both.
questions.realWorld: Term 'GEO' popularized by academic paper 'GEO: Generative Engine Optimization' (Aggarwal et al. 2023) + industry adoption 2024-2026. Cloudflare launched 'AI Audit' 2024. Google Search Console added 'AI Overviews' metrics 2024. Multiple SEO agencies pivoted to GEO/AEO services 2024-2025.

references.title: Aggarwal et al. — GEO: Generative Engine Optimization (2023)

questions.scenario: Tu web team pregunta: '¿debemos permitir o bloquear crawlers de IA? Y cuáles son?'. Lista: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, CCBot, Bytespider, anthropic-ai (deprecated).
questions.question: ¿Cómo se gestionan los crawlers de IA en robots.txt y cuál es la estrategia?

options.text: Cada AI vendor publica su crawler user-agent. Manageable en robots.txt: (1) GPTBot — OpenAI (training + search); ChatGPT-User (browsing on behalf of user); OAI-SearchBot (ChatGPT search); (2) ClaudeBot — Anthropic (training); claude-web (browsing); (3) Google-Extended — controls if content used for Bard/Gemini training (separate from Googlebot); (4) PerplexityBot — Perplexity indexing; (5) CCBot — Common Crawl (many models train on this); (6) Bytespider — ByteDance/TikTok. Estrategia: (a) ALLOW crawlers que drive traffic (Perplexity, ChatGPT search) — potential referral traffic; (b) BLOCK training crawlers si no quieres your content en modelos (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot); (c) DECISION per crawler, not blanket.
options.why: Correcto. Es la estrategia recomendada 2026. Cada crawler distinct purpose (training vs search-time browsing). Blocking training may reduce contribution to models pero doesn't guarantee — CCBot alimenta a many. Allowing search-time crawlers ofrece potential traffic. Decision informada, no blanket.

options.text: Bloquear todos los crawlers de IA para proteger contenido.
options.why: Extreme. Bloqueas también los que drive traffic (Perplexity search sends referrals). Y ausentarte de AI responses = invisibility para audience que usa AI.

options.text: Permitir todos; blocking es fútil.
options.why: Es una decisión estratégica valid. Para content premium/paywalled, blocking training makes sense. NYT vs OpenAI is exactly about unauthorized training.

options.text: robots.txt es advisory; los crawlers ignoran.
options.why: Los major players (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity) respetan robots.txt publicly. Some others (Bytespider historically) have been reported to ignore — but industry convention is respect.

questions.explanation: AI crawler list y purpose (2026): (1) OpenAI — GPTBot (training), ChatGPT-User (on-behalf browsing), OAI-SearchBot (ChatGPT search index); (2) Anthropic — ClaudeBot (training), claude-web (browsing); anthropic-ai deprecated; (3) Google — Google-Extended (Bard/Gemini training, separate from Googlebot for search); (4) Perplexity — PerplexityBot; (5) Common Crawl — CCBot (many models train on CC dumps); (6) ByteDance — Bytespider; (7) Applebot-Extended — Apple Intelligence; (8) Meta-ExternalAgent — Meta AI; (9) DuckAssistBot — DuckDuckGo. robots.txt syntax: User-agent: GPTBot / Disallow: /. Estrategia decisión por crawler: (a) block training if premium content; (b) allow search-time if want traffic; (c) monitor referrer analytics for AI referrals. Cloudflare AI Audit gives visibility.
questions.realWorld: NYT blocks GPTBot (2023). Reddit deals with OpenAI ($60M/year) y Google — content licensing. Stack Overflow blocks GPTBot pero has OpenAI partnership. Wikipedia allows all (public knowledge mission). Many news publishers block after Aug 2023 GPTBot introduction. Cloudflare launched AI Audit 2024, one-click block AI crawlers 2024.

questions.scenario: Un dev propone añadir 'llms.txt' a tu sitio. Pregunta: '¿es un standard? ¿ayuda a que ChatGPT lea nuestros docs mejor?'.
questions.question: ¿Qué es llms.txt, quién lo propuso, y cuál es su estado en 2026?

options.text: llms.txt es propuesta (Jeremy Howard / Answer.AI, Sep 2024) de archivo estándar (like robots.txt) que provee versión Markdown-formatted condensed del contenido del sitio, específicamente para LLM crawlers/agents. Ubicación: /llms.txt en raíz. Contiene: overview + curated links to important pages en Markdown. Propuesta relacionada: pages disponibles a URL + .md sufijo (foo.html.md). Estado 2026: NO oficialmente adopted por AI vendors (no confirmed ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity honor it), pero increasingly adopted por sites como de-facto convención GEO. Es best-practice signal, no guarantee de mejor citation.
options.why: Correcto. llms.txt es propuesta comunitaria (no W3C/IETF standard). Adoption creciente entre sites (Anthropic, Cloudflare, muchos SaaS have it). Impact medible en citation frequency es debated. Los vendors no publicly confirm honoring, pero best practice para GEO en 2026.

options.text: llms.txt es standard oficial W3C obligatorio.
options.why: Falso. Es propuesta community-driven, no standards body. No mandatory.

options.text: llms.txt reemplaza robots.txt.
options.why: Falso. Purpose distinto. robots.txt controls crawling; llms.txt provides curated content for LLM consumption. Complementary.

options.text: llms.txt no sirve para nada.
options.why: Prematuro. Adoption growing, guías de GEO 2026 recommend. Impact incierto pero probable ayuda a discoverability por AI agents. Cost bajo, potential benefit.

questions.explanation: llms.txt proposal (Jeremy Howard, Answer.AI, Sept 2024): archivo Markdown en /llms.txt en raíz del sitio. Rationale: robots.txt was built for search crawlers (allow/deny); llms.txt provides POSITIVE content for LLM agents (curated overview + links). Format: H1 con nombre del proyecto, blockquote con summary, sections con important pages linked. Related: .md versions of pages (foo.html.md as clean Markdown). Adoption 2026: Anthropic docs, Cloudflare, Perplexity, Nextra sites, Cursor, many SaaS. Vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic) haven't publicly confirmed honoring, but Answer.AI reports positive signal. Alternative/complementary: schema.org markup, JSON-LD, clean semantic HTML. Not a silver bullet — cited studies show impact varies.
questions.realWorld: llms.txt directory (llmstxt.org) lists adopters — thousands by 2026. Cloudflare added auto-generation for Workers Sites (2024). Vercel similar. Anthropic serves llms.txt at anthropic.com/llms.txt. Some SEO tools now check for llms.txt as GEO signal.

questions.scenario: Tu content page tiene: JavaScript-rendered content, no headers structured, no schema.org markup, no dates visible, no FAQ format, tables como imágenes. Tu marketing quiere aparecer en Perplexity y ChatGPT search.
questions.question: ¿Qué cambios técnicos maximizan probabilidad de citation por AI?

options.text: Priorities: (1) SERVER-SIDE RENDERING or SSG — AI crawlers may not execute JS reliably; HTML must contain content sin JS; (2) SEMANTIC HTML — <article>, <section>, <h1>-<h6>, <table>, <ul>; (3) SCHEMA.ORG structured data (JSON-LD) — Article, FAQ, HowTo, Product, Organization; (4) FAQ format (question-answer pairs, ideal para citation snippets); (5) DATES visible (published, updated) — freshness signal; (6) CITABLE facts (numbers, quotes, definitions) — con context, no orphan; (7) llms.txt para curated overview; (8) FAST loading (Core Web Vitals) — crawlers may timeout on slow sites.
options.why: Correcto. Es checklist técnica standard de GEO 2026. Cada elemento hace más parseable/citable content por AI. Skipear cualquiera reduce visibility. JS-only rendering es killer #1 (parcialmente resuelto con headless browsers pero unreliable).

options.text: Solo importa contenido de calidad; technical no importa.
options.why: Falso. Content invisible to crawlers (JS-only) = no citation. Structure + technical amplify calidad.

options.text: Copiar keywords múltiples veces mejora GEO.
options.why: Falso. Keyword stuffing es anti-pattern (era SEO 2005). AI models son mejor at semantic understanding; stuffing reduce quality signal.

options.text: Solo JSON API endpoints, no HTML.
options.why: Los crawlers principalmente parse HTML. Y JSON APIs sin discovery no reachable. HTML + schema.org es el path.

questions.explanation: GEO technical checklist: (1) RENDERING — SSR (Next.js, Nuxt) o SSG (Astro, Hugo) — content en HTML source no post-JS; (2) SEMANTIC HTML — <article>, <section>, <h1-6>, <table>, <ul>; (3) SCHEMA.ORG JSON-LD — Article, FAQ, HowTo, Product, Organization, Person, Event; (4) FAQ format for common questions; (5) DATES prominent (datePublished, dateModified in schema); (6) HEADERS clara jerarquía (H1 título, H2 secciones); (7) TABLES nativas (no imágenes); (8) IMAGES con alt text; (9) URLs semánticas (/product/name vs /p?id=123); (10) INTERNAL linking; (11) llms.txt; (12) CORE WEB VITALS bien (crawlers may timeout); (13) MOBILE responsive; (14) SITEMAP.xml. Anti-patterns: JS-only rendering, walls of text without structure, absent dates, image-as-text.
questions.realWorld: Wikipedia dominates AI citations because: SSR, semantic HTML, clear structure, citations of own, updates dated. Reddit citations increasing because: text-based, structured (posts, comments), high signal. Sites que migrated a SSR post-2024 (many SaaS) reported citation increase. Google Search Central guidelines for AI Overviews echo GEO principles.

questions.scenario: Tu blog está posted, structured, indexed. Pero no aparece en AI responses. Un consultor GEO dice: 'el contenido no es citation-worthy'.
questions.question: ¿Qué hace un contenido 'citation-worthy' desde POV de un LLM?

options.text: Citation-worthy content characteristics: (1) ORIGINAL data/research/insights — models prefieren sources primarias; (2) EXPERT quotes con attribution (nombre, credencial); (3) CONCRETE numbers/statistics con source; (4) UPDATED dates visible (recency signal); (5) UNIQUE angle (no rehash de content común); (6) AUTHORITATIVE domain (backlinks quality > quantity); (7) DEPTH — long-form thorough > shallow; (8) SPECIFIC (nombres, fechas, casos) > generic; (9) BALANCED (no clickbait, no over-promotional); (10) STRUCTURED (headers, lists, tables). Anti-patterns: AI-generated slop, rewrite/summary de otros, thin content, promotional-only.
options.why: Correcto. Los AI models priorizan sources con signal alta. Original + authoritative + fresh + specific = high citation. AI-generated slop es específicamente lo que AI evita (feedback loop — quality decrease if AI cites AI cites AI). 'E-E-A-T' (Google's Experience, Expertise, Authority, Trust) principles transfer to GEO.

options.text: Publicar más content aumenta citations proporcionalmente.
options.why: Falso. Volume sin quality no cita. Y podría diluir authority signal. Quality > quantity.

options.text: Copy Wikipedia content — es citation-worthy.
options.why: Duplicated content no cited. Wikipedia es citado por original + curation, no copiar mueve el needle.

options.text: Solo importa domain authority; content secondary.
options.why: Ambos importan. Domain authority ayuda pero low-quality content en alto authority site no citará. Content quality is the signal at end of day.

questions.explanation: Citation-worthy signals: (1) ORIGINAL research/data — surveys, benchmarks, case studies; (2) EXPERT quotes con names, credentials; (3) NUMBERS + statistics con sources; (4) DATES prominent (publication, updates); (5) UNIQUE perspective/angle; (6) DOMAIN authority (backlinks, mentions on trusted sites); (7) DEPTH (long-form comprehensive > listicle); (8) SPECIFICITY (concrete examples, named entities, dates, places); (9) BALANCE (no clickbait, acknowledge trade-offs); (10) STRUCTURED (headers, tables, bullet lists — easier extraction). Google's E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trust) principles apply. Anti-patterns: (a) AI-generated 'slop' content (Google demoting 2024); (b) content farms; (c) thin content; (d) over-promotional; (e) affiliate spam.
questions.realWorld: Stack Overflow answers frequently cited by AI (structure, expertise, votes). Academic papers cited more (original research). GitHub READMEs cited for code (canonical). NYT, Guardian, BBC cited for news (authority). Reddit cited for opinions/experiences (authenticity). Blogs of experts cited more than random content mills.

references.title: Google Search Central — E-E-A-T Quality Rater Guidelines

questions.scenario: Tu product B2B es unknown en AI answers. Marketing pregunta: '¿podemos crear página Wikipedia? ¿Postear en Reddit? ¿StackOverflow?'.
questions.question: ¿Cuál es la estrategia legítima para aumentar presencia en fuentes de training?

options.text: Estrategia: (1) WIKIPEDIA — sí SI reúne notability criteria (independent reliable sources cover you); crear astroturf viola policy y risk deletion; conseguir cobertura press first, then Wiki page follows naturally; (2) REDDIT — participate authentically (relevant subs), NOT self-promotion; users may organically mention product; buy Reddit ads legitimate; (3) STACKOVERFLOW — quality answers to questions where your tool applies; NOT spammy self-promotion; (4) HACKER NEWS — thoughtful launch posts, technical content; (5) DEV.TO, MEDIUM — technical content by experts; (6) GITHUB — open source contributions visible. All: authentic > manufactured. Manufactured presence gets penalized (Google demotion, subreddit bans, Wiki deletion).
options.why: Correcto. Estrategia sostenible: authentic contribution > manufactured presence. Los AI models train on Wikipedia, Reddit, StackOverflow, GitHub, blogs — high-signal sources. Authentic contribution builds long-term citations. Astroturf, spam, manufactured content are: (a) violating platform policies (bans); (b) detectable by AI/moderation increasingly; (c) risky legally (FTC endorsement guidelines).

options.text: Crear Wikipedia page de la empresa siempre es fácil.
options.why: Falso. Wikipedia has strict notability guidelines (WP:CORP). Companies without press coverage get deleted. Astroturf pages get deleted + editors banned.

options.text: Spam Reddit con posts de tu product para crear presence.
options.why: Contraproducente. Reddit subs ban self-promoters. Ambient hostility. Y AI models may detect promotional pattern and de-weight.

options.text: Pagar people para postear positive content.
options.why: FTC endorsement guidelines require disclosure. Undisclosed is deceptive. Platforms ban for manipulation. Reputational and legal risk.

questions.explanation: AI training data sources (major): Common Crawl (web), Wikipedia, Reddit, StackOverflow, GitHub, arXiv, books, licensed content (news deals). Presence en ellos amplifies your citation likelihood. Legitimate strategies: (1) EARNED media (PR, mentions) — leads to Wikipedia notability; (2) AUTHENTIC community participation — engineers answering StackOverflow, GitHub OSS; (3) THOUGHT leadership — blogs, HN posts, conference talks; (4) LICENSED content deals (large scale); (5) NEWS coverage via genuine story. Anti-strategies: (a) Astroturf; (b) undisclosed influencer; (c) content farms; (d) fake reviews; (e) Wikipedia editing by paid editors sin disclosure (WP:PAID violates). Long term, authentic > manufactured — AI + humans detecting manipulation increasingly.
questions.realWorld: OpenAI deals: AP, Axel Springer, News Corp, FT, Financial Times, Vox Media. Reddit deal $60M/year with Google. Anthropic settlements/deals. Growing 'zero-click' problem: AI answers reduce click-through to sources — many publishers negotiating compensation.

questions.scenario: Un customer report: 'le pregunté a ChatGPT sobre tu product y mencionó ventajas de tu competitor'. Investigas: tu página no está bien indexada; el competitor tiene comparison pages que rankeaban.
questions.question: ¿Qué es 'hallucination hijacking' y cómo se defiende?

options.text: Hallucination hijacking (o 'AI SEO poisoning'): competitor menciones tu brand en su content de tal forma que AI models associate their advantages con tu name, o worse, mention tu product como inferior en comparison content. Defense: (1) OWN your narrative — pages own comparativas actualizadas ('X vs Y' donde X es tu product); (2) BRAND presence en trusted sources; (3) MONITOR AI responses periodically ('Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude asking about your brand'); (4) STRUCTURED product info (schema.org Product, features, differentiators); (5) COUNTERACT hijacking con updated correct info published widely; (6) LEGAL avenues si defamation.
options.why: Correcto. Es fenómeno emergente. Los AI models synthesize from web content — si narrativa está en competitor's control, tu product suffers. Defense multi-nivel: own comparison content, monitor mentions, structured data claro, brand presence widespread. Es GEO combat.

options.text: No hay defensa; AI models son opaque.
options.why: Defensas existen (own narrative, structured data, monitoring). No es todo o nada.

options.text: Simplemente demandar al competitor.
options.why: Legal es último resource, y para defamation must be false + damaging. Comparison content en good faith es legal. Better invest en own narrative.

options.text: Blocking AI crawlers evita el problema.
options.why: Falso. Block just makes yourself invisible; competitor mentions still crawled from THEIR site. Blocking is defensive not offensive.

questions.explanation: Hallucination hijacking / AI SEO poisoning: adversarial GEO where competitors shape AI narrative about your brand. Vectors: (1) COMPARISON PAGES — 'X vs Y' articles favoring competitor; (2) REVIEW SITES — biased reviews; (3) FALSE ATTRIBUTION — model conflates products; (4) OUTDATED INFO — old bad reviews dominate. Defenses: (1) OWN COMPARISON CONTENT (fair, updated); (2) SCHEMA.ORG Product markup claro; (3) BRAND PRESENCE en trusted sources (owned blog, press, docs); (4) MONITOR — periodic queries to Perplexity/ChatGPT/Claude with brand-related questions; (5) RESPOND — publish counter-narrative content; (6) TRACK — tools like Profound, Athena, Otterly monitor AI mentions. Emerging category: 'AI reputation management'.
questions.realWorld: Cases documented 2024-2025: brands finding themselves misrepresented in AI answers. Tools like Profound.ai, Otterly.ai, Athena launched to monitor brand mentions across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini. Legal cases: some defamation lawsuits against AI companies for false statements about individuals (Mark Walters vs OpenAI 2023, ongoing others).

questions.topic: Tracking — cómo saber que la IA te está citando
questions.scenario: Marketing pregunta 'quiero KPI de AI citations: ¿cuánto Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude nos citan?'. Analytics tradicional (Google Analytics) muestra referrer confuso.
questions.question: ¿Cómo medir citations por AI en 2026?

options.text: Methods: (1) REFERRER analytics — tráfico from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot etc identifiable en Google Analytics (referrer domains: chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com); increases 2024-2026; (2) MONITORING TOOLS — Profound, Otterly, Athena, BrandRank.ai query AI models periodically con brand-related questions y track mentions/positions; (3) DIRECT QUERIES — periodically ask ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity yourself about your brand + competitors; (4) SERVER LOGS — track AI crawler user-agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot) — indicates indexing; (5) CLOUDFLARE AI AUDIT — visibility into AI crawlers hitting your site; (6) LIMITATIONS — no ground truth, samples only, models change daily.
options.why: Correcto. Es measurement multi-method porque no hay single source of truth. Referrer + monitoring tools + direct queries + server logs = triangulation. Emerging category tools (Profound, Otterly) precisely para this. Limitaciones honestas: samples, no comprehensive, models change.

options.text: Imposible medir; los AI models son caja negra.
options.why: Existen métodos (referrer, monitoring tools). No es perfecto pero es measurable.

options.text: Solo importa Google Analytics referrer.
options.why: Insuficiente. Referrer only captures click-through — muchos users read AI answer sin click ('zero-click' problem). Necesitas monitoring tools para captar mentions sin click.

options.text: Contar backlinks es suficiente proxy.
options.why: Backlinks es SEO metric. AI citations is distinct — un site sin backlinks puede ser cited if quality content, y viceversa.

questions.explanation: AI citation tracking methods: (1) REFERRER analytics — Google Analytics 4, Adobe, Fathom capture referrer domains. AI referrer domains 2026: chatgpt.com, chat.openai.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com, claude.ai (limited browsing). Cloudflare Zaraz, Vercel Analytics native support; (2) MONITORING TOOLS — Profound.ai, Otterly.ai, Athena, BrandRank.ai automate querying AI models con brand questions, capture citations, rank positions; (3) DIRECT MANUAL queries periodically; (4) SERVER LOG analysis — track crawler user-agents; Cloudflare AI Audit dashboard; (5) SOCIAL LISTENING — mentions of 'ChatGPT told me...' referring to your product. Limitations: (a) sampling only; (b) models change frequently; (c) no ground truth from vendors (they don't disclose citation data); (d) 'zero-click' problem — AI answer without click is invisible to referrer.
questions.realWorld: Profound.ai launched 2024, raised Series A 2025. Otterly, Athena, BrandRank similar. Cloudflare AI Audit 2024 gives crawler visibility. Google Search Console added AI Overviews impressions 2024. Adobe Analytics added AI referrer categorization 2024. Big publishers (NYT, WaPo) invest in tracking to argue for AI compensation deals.

questions.scenario: Tu chatbot interfaz. Options: (a) empty textarea 'Ask anything'; (b) 4 suggested prompts chips ('¿Cómo hago X?', 'Explícame Y', 'Ayuda con Z'); (c) mix (chips + textarea); (d) guided flow con questions.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son los trade-offs y cuándo usar cada uno?

options.text: Trade-offs: (1) EMPTY textarea — flexibility máxima pero 'blank page problem' — users no saben qué preguntar; alta friction inicial; (2) SUGGESTED prompts — reduce friction, showcase capabilities, guide to successful use cases; risk: users think tool is limited to suggestions; (3) MIX (chips + textarea) — best of both; industry standard 2026 (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity landing show ambos); (4) GUIDED FLOW — para tasks estructuradas (form-filling, wizards); overhead para exploratory. Default: MIX with chips for discoverability + textarea for freedom.
options.why: Correcto. Chips + textarea es standard pattern. Chips solve blank page + showcase; textarea preserves flexibility. Guided flow apropiado para tasks estructuradas específicas (onboarding forms, structured queries). Empty textarea only funciona con power users que conocen el tool.

options.text: Empty textarea siempre; power users no necesitan hints.
options.why: Excludes new users, first-time interactions. Blank page problem is real. Chips reduce friction sin costo para power users (ignore them).

options.text: Solo chips; textarea confunde users.
options.why: Limits capabilities. Users con specific questions se frustran. Textarea es essential for flexibility.

options.text: Guided flow siempre; users prefieren estructura.
options.why: Guided flow es correcto para specific structured tasks (onboarding, forms). Para general purpose chat, es fricción excessive.

questions.explanation: Chat UI patterns: (1) EMPTY textarea 'Ask anything' — max flexibility, blank page problem for new users, higher abandonment; (2) SUGGESTED PROMPTS (chips/buttons) — reduce friction, showcase use cases, but risk of 'limited to suggestions' perception; (3) MIX chips + textarea — industry standard 2026 (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity landing show 3-6 suggested prompts + empty textarea); (4) GUIDED FLOW / WIZARD — questions with predefined options, then textarea for details — good for structured tasks (booking, forms); (5) SLASH COMMANDS / MODES — power user pattern (Claude Code /commands, Cursor /symbols); (6) HISTORY-BASED suggestions — 'continue previous chat about X'. Design: measure first-message success rate (do users get useful response first try?). Suggested prompts often 20-40% first-message uplift.
questions.realWorld: ChatGPT landing has 4 suggested prompts + textarea. Claude.ai similar. Perplexity shows trending queries. Gemini shows contextual suggestions. Cursor Chat shows / commands. Enterprise chatbots (Salesforce Einstein) often use guided flow for structured workflows.

references.title: Nielsen Norman — AI chatbot UX patterns

questions.topic: Klarna AI, Perplexity vs NYT — casos famosos
questions.scenario: Un exec pregunta: '¿qué lecciones sacar de los casos famosos AI 2023-2026? Klarna's chatbot, Perplexity vs NYT, Devin, Cursor pricing, EU AI Act enforcement Aug 2026, etc.'.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son las lecciones estratégicas más importantes de casos recientes?

options.text: Lecciones: (1) KLARNA AI chatbot (2024) — announced 700 human jobs replaced; después 2024 rectified — quality issues, brought back humans; LESSON: hype outpaces reality, human-in-loop crucial; (2) DEVIN benchmarks vs realidad (Answer.ai critique 2024) — LESSON: benchmarks ≠ real work; pilot in your codebase; (3) CURSOR pricing removal $30 unlimited (2024) — LESSON: vendor pricing volatile, plan for changes, avoid lock-in; (4) PERPLEXITY vs NYT/publishers — legal disputes over content use — LESSON: copyright unclear, respect opt-outs; (5) EU AI ACT enforcement Aug 2026 — LESSON: regulation is real, plan compliance ahead; (6) OPENAI outages, Anthropic capacity issues 2024 — LESSON: multi-provider strategy essential; (7) GOOGLE AI OVERVIEWS 'glue on pizza' (2024) — LESSON: quality of sources matters, hallucinations expensive.
options.why: Correcto. Las lecciones son concretas y aplicables: (1) hype ≠ reality; (2) benchmarks limited; (3) vendor volatile; (4) legal ambiguity; (5) regulation active; (6) redundancy needed; (7) source quality matters. Todos casos documentados en press y post-mortems industry.

options.text: AI ya no importa; industry en decline.
options.why: Falso. Industry growing, adoption growing. Los casos son adjustments, not decline. Companies learning from mistakes.

options.text: Todos los casos son propaganda; ignore.
options.why: Falso. Son documented cases con post-mortems, legal filings, financial reports. Ignoring learn lessons is expensive.

options.text: Solo relevantes en US; no aplican a Europa.
options.why: Falso. Muchos son global (Klarna Suecia, Perplexity US pero sued globally, EU AI Act aplicable a global vendors operating en EU).

questions.explanation: Casos famosos y lecciones: (1) KLARNA AI chatbot — 700 jobs 'replaced' 2024, backtrack 2024-2025 due quality/CX issues; lesson: hype outpaces reality, human oversight matters; (2) DEVIN (Cognition) — impressive demos 2024, Answer.ai critique showed <20% real success; lesson: benchmarks limited, pilot required; (3) CURSOR pricing — removed unlimited tier 2024, community backlash; lesson: vendor pricing volatile, diversify; (4) PERPLEXITY vs NYT, WSJ, Forbes — 'anti-plagiarism' letters 2024, content scraping disputes; lesson: copyright uncertain, negotiate deals; (5) EU AI ACT Aug 2026 enforcement — Article 50 transparency, high-risk obligations; lesson: compliance is real; (6) OPENAI outages Nov 2023, capacity throttling 2024; ANTHROPIC context issues; lesson: multi-provider strategy; (7) GOOGLE AI OVERVIEWS 'glue on pizza' 'eat one small rock a day' May 2024 — sourced Reddit jokes; lesson: source quality matters; (8) SAMSUNG banning ChatGPT after leaks 2023; lesson: data leaks real; (9) NYT vs OpenAI ongoing since Dec 2023; lesson: legal risk; (10) AIR CANADA chatbot lawsuit 2024 — court held company liable for chatbot's incorrect refund info; lesson: legal responsibility for AI outputs.
questions.realWorld: Todos los casos documentados en press mainstream + industry press + court filings. Klarna announcements 2024 tracked publicly. Answer.ai Devin post is canonical reference. Air Canada v Moffatt 2024 (BC Civil Resolution Tribunal) set precedent for chatbot liability. NYT v OpenAI complaint public + discovery ongoing.
